name: Oliver Herford
credit: Portrait of Oliver Herford (photograph, c. 1916) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Oliver Herford (1863–1935) was an English-born American humorist, illustrator and writer of light verse.
He wrote and drew many small books of whimsy, such as The Bashful Earthquake (1898).

poems.title: Earth
poems.author: Oliver Herford
poems.text:
If this little world to-night
  Suddenly should fall through space
In a hissing, headlong flight,
  Shrivelling from off its face,
As it falls into the sun,
  In an instant every trace
Of the little crawling things—
  Ants, philosophers, and lice,
Cattle, cockroaches, and kings,
  Beggars, millionaires, and mice,
Men and maggots all as one
As it falls into the sun....
Who can say but at the same
  Instant from some planet far,
A child may watch us and exclaim:
  “See the pretty shooting star!”

poems.title: The Elf and the Dormouse
poems.author: Oliver Herford
poems.text:
Under a toadstool crept a wee Elf,
Out of the rain to shelter himself.

Under the toadstool, sound asleep,
Sat a big Dormouse all in a heap.

Trembled the wee Elf, frightened and yet
Fearing to fly away lest he get wet.

To the next shelter—maybe a mile!
Sudden the wee Elf smiled a wee smile.

Tugged till the toadstool toppled in two.
Holding it over him, gaily he flew.

Soon he was safe home, dry as could be.
Soon woke the Dormouse—“Good gracious me!

“Where is my toadstool?” loud he lamented.
—And that’s how umbrellas first were invented.
